name: Vicente del Bosque
scopeNote: Counted spells: Real Madrid (Nov 1999 - Jun 2003: Champions League 2000 and 2002, La Liga 2001 and 2003) and Spain (Jul 2008 - Jul 2016: World Cup 2010, Euro 2012). Exact start/end days are not in the mined pages (only month-level: 'noviembre del 99', 'noviembre de 1999' in the Flashscore question, 'July 2016' via search results); day-level values in spellsCounted are approximate and flagged in openQuestions. Style term used by sources: possession football / 'tiki-taka' inherited from Luis Aragonés and refined with a double pivot (Busquets + Xabi Alonso); 4-6-0 without striker at Euro 2012. At Madrid: back three won the 2000 Champions League, then 4-4-2. Tactical coverage of Madrid is thin (mostly his own retrospective interviews); Spain is better covered. Excluded spells carry year-only dates because sources give only years (1994 for two months, 1996, Beşiktaş 2004-05).
openQuestions: Spell day-level dates: Madrid start 1999-11-17 inferred (Periodico de Ibiza 1999-11-18 says the club welcomes him 'hoy'; day from memory/search, not mined text); Madrid end 2003-06-24 from Irish Times article date; Spain start 2008-07-15 and end 2016-07-04 (football-espana URL date) not confirmed in mined pages.

Interim stints at Real Madrid (1994, 1996) excluded: no tactical coverage found, brief caretaker spells with fewer than 15 matches; El Gráfico quote ('se dio un interinato, y luego otro') confirms they were interim. Beşiktaş 2004-05 excluded: no major titles, no tactical coverage found, and it did not lead to a bigger job.
Marking system (zonal vs man) not found for Del Bosque teams in any mined page; only a search summary mentioned Germany's zonal marking at a 2010 corner (unverified).
Real Madrid sources are mostly his own retrospective interviews (2024-25): treat as retrospective; no contemporary tactical analysis was mined for 1999-2003.
Popular label 'tiki-taka' is Aragonés/Barcelona heritage; Del Bosque said 'We don't have a magic formula, we have a plan based on the players that we have available' (2014).
Spanish press framing of Florentino Pérez's 2003 dismissal ('librillo muy tradicional') is the club's view, not neutral evidence of his style.
Dressing-room crisis Barcelona-Real Madrid (2010) covered only by a Coaches' Voice podcast blurb, not the interview itself.

Tactical trade-offs: These Football Times describes 'a tactical masterclass' with a back three at Old Trafford (April 2000), while Coaches' Voice says the back three was used to win the 1999/2000 Champions League; the 4-4-2 vs 4-1-3-2 diamond label for 2001/02 differs between his own words (4-4-2) and TFT (4-1-3-2).
Source on the 1994 and 1996 interim spells kept as verified:false because it falls outside the counted spells (it documents the exclusion).
